entries.10cfff3fddda84f0: A reportable segment that manufactures and sells automotive parts in the United States and Mexico. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥77,591 million. Sales including inter-segment internal sales were ¥77,657 million (up 0.3% year on year), and operating profit was ¥4,402 million (down 38.5%). The securities report attributes the increase in sales to an increase in sales volume, and the decrease in operating profit to an increase in various expenses. In Mexico, because changes in the business environment meant the profit originally expected could no longer be anticipated, the carrying amounts of fixed assets such as automotive parts manufacturing equipment were reduced to their recoverable amounts, and an impairment loss of ¥1,805 million was recorded as an extraordinary loss. Franklin Precision Industry, Inc., a consolidated subsidiary in this segment, accounted for more than 10% of consolidated sales, with sales of ¥34,211 million (excluding inter-segment sales).

entries.52f51a2f72def1d4: A reportable segment based in the Czech Republic, France and Belgium. Sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥16,251 million. The securities report attributes the increase in sales to the effect of exchange rates, and the decrease in operating profit to an increase in various expenses. Manufacturing and sales are carried out by Aisan Industry Czech s.r.o. in the Czech Republic, and Aisan Corporation Europe S.A. in Belgium is the base for sales activities in Europe. entries.5736aaea54440427: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥18,287 million (down 0.3% year on year), ordinary profit was ¥19,229 million (down 0.3%), and net income attributable to owners of the parent was ¥13,074 million (down 1.2%). Operating profit by region was ¥3,160 million in Japan (up 36.3%), ¥9,366 million in Asia (up 20.0%), ¥4,402 million in the Americas (down 38.5%) and ¥1,180 million in Europe (down 8.4%). In the Americas, because changes in the business environment meant that the revenue originally expected from automotive parts manufacturing facilities in Mexico could no longer be anticipated, an impairment loss of ¥1,805 million was recorded as an extraordinary loss. Net cash provided by operating activities was ¥7,204 million, a decrease of ¥21,018 million from the previous year.
